images.filename: Bundesarchiv Bild 183-L19397, Lettland, Riga, Begrüßung der deutschen Soldaten.jpg
images.caption:
For documentary purposes the German Federal Archive often retained the original image captions, which may be erroneous, biased, obsolete or politically extreme. Scherl Bilderdienst
Befreiungsjubel um die deutschen Soldaten in Riga.
Als die deutschen Truppen die Stadt Riga einnahmen, wurde die dortige Bevölkerung von einem Jubelsturm der Freude erfasst. Die Menschen, die monatelang unter dem Blutterror gelitten und sich in den letzten Wochen in den Kellern ihrer Häuser versteckt hatten, eilten nun auf die Straßen und Plätze und drängten sich, um die deutschen Soldaten zu begrüßen.

PK Lette,  7.7.41 [Herausgabedatum],

images.filename: Atlas Van der Hagen-KW1049B10 029-LIVONIA Vulgo Lyetland.jpeg
images.caption: This map depicts the Baltic states Latvia and Estonia. Ever since the Treaty of Altmar in 1629 this area was a Swedish province which was mainly inhabited by Germans. The map was published in 1662 in the second volume of Joan Blaeus Atlas Maior. As a basis for this map, Blaeu used a large-size wall map from the Swedish scientist Anders Bureus (1571-1661), who was head of the topographical survey.
images.alt: This map depicts the Baltic states Latvia and Estonia. Ever since the Treaty of Altmar in 1629 this area was a Swedish province which was mainly inhabited by Germans. The map was published in 1662 in the second volume of Joan Blaeus Atlas Maior. As a basis for this map, Blaeu used a large-size wall map from the Swedish scientist Anders Bureus (1571-1661), who was head of the topographical survey.
